points.summary: Mitchell Berman pledges to raise the federal minimum wage, crack down on rent-price fixing and hidden junk fees, lower child care costs, expand the child tax credit, expand the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit, roll back tariffs on lumber, and prevent private equity from buying single-family homes.
points.quote: Raise the federal minimum wage so that working a full time job can support a family

points.summary: Berman proposes restoring ACA subsidies, reversing Medicaid cuts, creating a public option, capping out-of-pocket prescription drug costs, making $35 insulin available, requiring faster prior authorization decisions, stopping private equity from buying hospitals, and expanding mental health and addiction treatment.
points.quote: Create a public option so families have a real choice and insurers have to compete on price

points.summary: Berman commits to overturning Citizens United, ending dark money, passing a stock trading ban for Congress, the president, and vice president, closing the revolving door between Congress and lobbying firms, and imposing ethics rules on Supreme Court Justices.
points.quote: Pass a real ban on stock trading by members of Congress, the president, and the vice president.

points.summary: Berman supports passing the PRO Act to protect union organizing rights, prioritizing federal contracts for companies that hire locally, stopping subsidies for companies that move jobs overseas, and expanding apprenticeships in skilled trades so a good career does not require a four-year degree.
points.quote: Pass the PRO Act to protect the right to organize, and hold employers accountable when they retaliate against workers for trying to form a union

points.summary: Berman calls for Congress to uphold the War Powers Act, end what he describes as the costly, reckless war in Iran, and reduce the costs of war and high prices borne by Wisconsin families.
points.quote: We should end the costly, reckless war in Iran and bring down the costs of war and high prices that Wisconsin families are shouldering.

points.summary: Berman states that healthcare decisions belong to patients, that politicians should not interfere between a woman and her doctor, and that rural maternity care and Medicaid reimbursement rates must be addressed to keep labor and delivery units open.
points.quote: Politicians should not be getting in between a woman and her doctor.

points.summary: Berman pledges to fully fund public schools, restore the value of Pell Grants, invest in technical and vocational training, and protect the Department of Education from efforts to dismantle it.
points.quote: We need to fully fund our public schools, restore the value of Pell Grants, and invest in technical and vocational training.

points.summary: Berman supports investing in clean energy, building a resilient grid, protecting Lake Michigan and drinking water, cleaning up PFAS, making polluters pay, holding data center companies accountable for energy and water costs, and protecting public lands from drilling, mining, and logging.
points.quote: protect Lake Michigan and our drinking water from contamination, clean up PFAS, and make the polluters pay for it
